'''Niky Kamran''' {{post-nominal|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born May 22, 1959) is a [[Belgians|Belgian]] and [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] whose research concerns [[geometric analysis]], [[differential geometry]], and [[mathematical physics]].<ref name="pims">{{citation|url=http://www.pims.math.ca/news/2014-crm-fields-pims-prize-winner-niky-kamran|title=2014 CRM - Fields - PIMS Prize Winner: Niky Kamran|publisher=[[Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences]]|accessdate=2015-02-08}}</ref> He is a Distinguished James McGill Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at [[McGill University]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://www.math.mcgill.ca/nkamran/CVShortJan2019.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|year=2019|accessdate=2019-02-23}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Kamran was born in [[Brussels]], Belgium. He earned a [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] in mathematics from the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] in 1980.<ref name="cv" /> He moved to Canada for graduate studies, earning a [[Ph.D.]] in 1984 from the [[University of Waterloo]]; his dissertation, titled ''Contributions to the Study of the Separation of Variables and Symmetry Operators for Relativistic Wave Equations on Curved Spacetime'', was jointly supervised by [[Raymond McLenaghan|Raymond G. McLenaghan]] and Robert Debever.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=67885}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1986 he became an assistant professor at Waterloo but then, after spending a year as a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], Princeton, New Jersey, he moved to McGill in 1989. He was promoted to full professor in 1995, was awarded a James McGill Professorship in 2003 which he held until 2024, after which he was named Distinguished James McGill Professor as of 2024.<ref name="cv" />

Kamran won the [[Aisenstadt Prize]] in 1992.<ref>{{citation|url=http://crm.umontreal.ca/prix/prix_Aisenstadt_an.html|title=Aisenstadt Prize recipients|publisher=CRM|accessdate=2015-02-08|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304063820/http://crm.umontreal.ca/prix/prix_Aisenstadt_an.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]]<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.rsc.ca/en/search-fellows|title=Fellows directory|publisher=[[Royal Society of Canada]]|accessdate=2019-10-25|archive-date=2017-06-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170610224856/http://www.rsc.ca/en/search-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 2002 and was awarded a [[The Killam Trusts|Killam]] Fellowship from 2006 to 2008.<ref>{{citation|url=https://killamprogram.canadacouncil.ca/-/media/Files/Killam/Laureates/KillamProgramLaureates.xlsx|title=Killam Program Past Recipients|accessdate=2019-10-25|archive-date=2019-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191025214136/https://killamprogram.canadacouncil.ca/-/media/Files/Killam/Laureates/KillamProgramLaureates.xlsx|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, he became one of the inaugural Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2015-02-08|archive-date=2018-08-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2014, Kamran was the winner of the [[CRM-Fields-PIMS prize]],<ref name="pims" /> and in 2019 he was elected a member of the [[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.academieroyale.be/fr/who-who-detail/relations/niky-kamran/|title=Niky Kamran|work=Who's who|publisher=[[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium ]]|accessdate=2019-10-25}}</ref> That same academy had awarded him in 1988 the mathematics prize of its annual competition for a memoir on the equivalence problem of [[Élie Cartan]] and its applications.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mémoires de l'Académie royale de Belgique|url=http://www.academieroyale.be/fr/publications-academie-toutes-publications-detail/oeuvres-2/contributions-to-the-study-of-the-equivalence-problem-of-elie-cartan-an-its-applications-to-partial-and-ordinary-differential-equations/|publication-date=}}</ref>
